items.title_found: Brain implants, software guide speech-disabled person’s intended words to computer screen
items.meta_description: Our brains remember how to formulate words even if the muscles responsible for saying them out loud are incapacitated. A brain-computer hookup is making the dream of restoring speech a reality.
passages: On March 29, 2022, a Stanford Medicine neurosurgeon placed two tiny sensors apiece in two separate regions - both implicated in speech production - along the surface of Bennett's brain.

Pat Bennett has lost her ability to speak because of ALS.Steve Fisch "These initial results have proven the concept, and eventually technology will catch up to make it easily accessible to people who cannot speak," Bennett wrote.

The devices transmit signals from a couple of speech-related regions in Bennett’s brain to state-of-the-art software that decodes her brain activity and converts it to text displayed on a computer screen.
Find more photos here (credit: Steve Fisch/Stanford Medicine).
“But in a group of ALS patients, it begins with speech difficulties.
Combined with state-of-the-art decoding software, they're designed to translate the brain activity accompanying attempts at speech into words on a screen.

passages: NEWS AND VIEWS 23 August 2023 Brain implants that enable speech pass performance milestones Two brain–computer interfaces have been developed that bring unprecedented capabilities for translating brain signals into sentences — at speeds close to that of normal speech, and with vocabularies exceeding 1,000 words.

Two articles published in Nature demonstrate that individuals who are unable to speak as a result of severe paralysis could potentially use implantable brain–computer interfaces (BCIs) to communicate at rates much greater than those typically achievable with alternative communication options.
